root_cause_label: Truncated Training Data and Naive Uniform Negative Sampling
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent deliberately truncated training data to 500k samples and adopted naive uniform negative sampling to circumvent slow training, producing embeddings too poor to pass any semantic analogy test.
t_err_evidence: In step 18, the agent rewrites create_training_data to add max_samples=1000000 parameter (later set to 500000 in step 20) and in step 19 replaces negative sampling with uniform random choice — decisive shortcuts that guarantee insufficient embedding quality.
t_commit_evidence: Step 20 hard-codes max_samples=500000 in train_word2vec, locking in both the data truncation and the uniform negative sampling strategy; from this point the agent proceeds straight to training without reconsidering the approach.
t_surface_evidence: Step 22 shows all five analogy tests failing: king-man+queen returns ['queen','king','incidents'] instead of 'woman'; france-paris+japan returns ['france','japan','reliance'] instead of 'tokyo'; etc.
trigger_explanation: The agent saw slow training speed at step 16 (~27 it/s, ~71 minutes per epoch) and acted on the false premise that a 500k-sample subset with uniform negative sampling would still produce 'meaningful word embeddings' satisfying the task requirement — without verifying that claim before committing.
forewarning_evidence: Step 16 shows a UserWarning about slow tensor creation from numpy arrays and the training was projecting ~71 minutes per epoch; the agent interrupted at step 17. This performance signal warned that the full training was infeasible but the agent chose a data-truncation shortcut rather than an algorithmic fix.
fabrication_evidence: Steps 18-20 replace full-corpus training with a 500k-sample subset and trivial uniform negative sampling. Steps 23-28 then run analogy tests as if verifying success, but no attempt is made to retrain or fix the shortcut despite consistently failing analogy results.
